clue.text: Puts rumpled sheets away from mouth

indicators.note: rumpled bedding is disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away crumpled bedsheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumpled' looks like it describes the sheets, but it signals the anagram of 'Puts'; 'sheets' is a quantity of paper, and 'away from mouth' describes heading upriver.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upriver means heading toward the source, away from where a river meets the sea.

clue.text: Bird edges round cake crumb

parts.note: pie is an old word for the magpie

indicators.note: the edges running round the cake are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A bird pecks around the rim of a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a small fragment or bit of something, broken off a larger whole.

clue.text: Lead potentially has eider and gannet suffering

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters of the two bird names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lead poisoning afflicts two seabirds, an eider duck and a gannet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the toxic metal; it is the leading role an actress plays in a tragic drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress specialising in tragic roles could well be the star, the principal player, of a production.

clue.text: Model takes chance regularly for good ability to get results

indicators.note: the model takes in new letters in place of one it loses
for marks what is swapped out: the new letters stand for the abbreviation of good

parts.note: an effigy is a model or likeness of a person

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of chance, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A fashion model takes a chance now and again on her own ability.
explanation.walkthrough: CAC (every other letter of 'chance') replaces the G of EFFIGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficacy is effectiveness: the power to produce the intended outcome.

clue.text: Chap taking risks mostly on mountain ridge's eastern tongue

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: daring means bold, taking risks
a chine is a mountain ridge; the possessive adds the S

explanation.surface: A daring mountaineer on an eastern ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of DARING, leaving DARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue here means language; this is the standard spoken language of China.

clue.text: Note switches in random mutation?

indicators.note: the note switches in, taking the place of a letter of the word for random

parts.note: something done at random happens by chance
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A geneticist observes that one note changes in a random mutation.
explanation.walkthrough: G replaces the last C of CHANCE. The question mark flags mutation as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutation is an alteration, a kind of transformation, hence a fair example.

clue.text: Water-loving youngster — small seal, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a signet ring

explanation.surface: A young seal pup that loves the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a baby seal; 'seal' is the stamp on a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan, a bird that lives on rivers and lakes, is a water-loving juvenile.

clue.text: Decree agreement has no power

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An agreement without force behind it is toothless.
explanation.definitionFit: A law passed by a parliament, like an edict, is an official decree.

clue.text: PM's left without fellow ministers' support, ultimately

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one word sits around the others

parts.note: having left means having gone
a lad is a fellow

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A prime minister has been deserted by his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'ultimately' takes the final letter of both 'ministers'' and 'support'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was four times British Prime Minister in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Force confronted over drink

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: confronted means faced
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A force was confronted over a drink, perhaps in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns FACED into DECAF, then F is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with the caffeine removed is a common beverage.

clue.text: Near agreement, backing a last drink

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: backing says the word is read from back to front

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: Close to a deal, the negotiators toast it with a final glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink, often alcoholic, taken just before bed, the final one of the day.

clue.text: Married before once, and no more than

parts.note: ere is an old, once-used word for before

explanation.surface: Someone married before, once, and no more than that.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only, nothing beyond: a mere child is no more than a child.

clue.text: Caught bird by head, being a chicken?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the raven is a bird
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A bird is caught by its head; is it a chicken?
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird but means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chicken means being cowardly, and cowardice is the state of lacking courage.

clue.text: Man resounds with stirring operatic aria

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tenor's voice resounds with a stirring operatic aria.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's tenor showpiece from Turandot, made famous by Pavarotti, is a celebrated opera song.

clue.text: Mexican music from aria: Chinese, partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musicologist traces a Mexican style partly to a Chinese aria.
explanation.definitionFit: This is traditional Mexican folk music played by strolling bands with trumpets, violins and guitars.

clue.text: Attachment of a sheet enclosing pound note

indicators.note: enclosing says one part goes around the others

parts.note: a page is a sheet of a book
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A page encloses a banknote worth a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money; here it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or joined on to a larger thing, such as a limb.

clue.text: One working too hard pulls back

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tows means pulls

explanation.surface: An overworked person finally pulls back.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is someone, usually a student, who studies intensively, perhaps excessively.

clue.text: Not skilled in creation, missing out the third day

indicators.note: missing out the third says the third letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: creation can mean the whole universe

explanation.surface: Someone is not knowledgeable about the Creation story, skipping the third day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the third day' tempts the solver toward Genesis; the I of UNIVERSE is dropped, then D added.
explanation.definitionFit: Unversed in a subject means inexperienced or lacking knowledge of it.

clue.text: Passable old writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An old author is only passable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passable' means able to be passed through, not merely adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that is passable is clear, unobstructed, able to be travelled.

clue.text: Fun codes perplexed and puzzled

indicators.note: perplexed suggests tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cryptographer is baffled by playful ciphers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puzzled is being bewildered, unsure of what is going on.

clue.text: Socialist's gutted over widespread conflict

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: rife means widespread

explanation.surface: A socialist is gutted by widespread conflict in the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismay; it empties Socialist to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife means bitter disagreement or fighting.

clue.text: Lace still vino, putting in tons

indicators.note: putting in says one letter goes inside the others

parts.note: still means motionless, inert
vino is informal for wine

explanation.surface: Lace is placed alongside still wine, delivered by the ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still vino' suggests non-sparkling wine; still and vino are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace things together is to twist or weave them into one another.

clue.text: Wettish mark in person's home comes back

indicators.note: comes back says the whole is read backwards
in says one part goes inside the other

parts.note: pad is slang for someone's flat or home
M is the abbreviation for mark, as in the German currency

explanation.surface: A damp mark reappears in someone's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside PAD, and 'comes back' turns PMAD around.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp means slightly wet, moist.

clue.text: State of Slovenia mired in revolution, somewhat

indicators.note: in revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Slovenia is stuck in a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' hides ENIAM in 'Slovenia mired'; 'in revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a US state in New England, on the Canadian border.

clue.text: Place for first flowers presumably is in March

indicators.note: in says one part goes inside the other

parts.note: a parade is a march

explanation.surface: In March, the first spring blooms appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is a procession. The Garden of Eden would have held the first flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the Garden of Eden, so the original garden, where plants first grew.

clue.text: Suitable form of high-speed transport

definitions.meaning: the Advanced Passenger Train was an experimental British tilting train

explanation.surface: A suitable kind of fast transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting; the abbreviation names British Rail's tilting high-speed train.

clue.text: Chap after small snack

indicators.note: after places the man's name behind the abbreviation

parts.note: Arnie is a man's name, short for Arnold

explanation.surface: A man wants a little snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich, a light snack.

clue.text: View article and be very angry

parts.note: to view is to see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Reading a newspaper piece makes someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to fume, boiling with suppressed rage.

clue.text: Scrap what could be The Times inside page

parts.note: an end is a leftover scrap, as in odds and ends
The Times is an example of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Throw away the Times' inside page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside page' suggests a newspaper; it is a page pasted inside a book's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the blank leaf fixed inside the cover of a book.
